retention.stated: the disk persists while the plan is paid; a daily backup of the previous 24 hours is included and replicated three times in the same datacentre

chaining: a 4 GiB box with genuinely unmetered EU traffic, which makes it the one row here that can serve bytes rather than only compute

notes: CHANGED in shape, not in price. USD 4.54 a month is confirmed and it is the 12-month-upfront rate. But VPS-1 is 4 GB of RAM and 2 vCPU, not 8 GiB: it is under the line on price and under the beefy bar on memory, so it does not compete with the 8 GiB rows. It is listed because the incumbent row put it in this band and the shape is what disqualifies it. The next rung up, VPS-2 at USD 8.50, is 8 GB and 4 vCPU and over the line. Two things were not settled: the renewal after the 12-month term (the configurator that would show it refused to load), and whether VAT is added (the page prints no VAT line at all, and the 'World [$]' locale implies no EU VAT for a non-EU buyer). Worst case exposure is not computable without the renewal.

extras.term: 12 months upfront for the USD 4.54 figure
extras.price_arithmetic: USD 4.54 a month on the 12-month-upfront term ('pricing=upfront12' in the Configure link). x 12 = USD 54.48 out of pocket. It is a VPS, so no 730-hour multiplication. No conversion was needed: the page prints USD for the World locale.
extras.out_of_pocket_note: USD 54.48 is the vendor's own USD rate ($4.54) x 12 on the .com storefront. The EU catalogue price converts to USD 51.17. The two differ because OVHcloud's internal EUR/USD rate sits near 1.19, above the ECB 1.1193; the vendor's own USD figure is the one a buyer on the English site pays.
extras.renewal_note: not published on the pricing page. So the post-12-month price is unverified rather than absent.
